title: Specifications, quantities and costing
intro: A quantity file links drawings, materials, hardware and services. Build identifiable items with explicit units and a declared training cost model, then check revisions and double counting.
goals: Link part IDs to specifications and quantities
Calculate each line using matching units
Check scope and revision before issue

sections.title: Link part IDs to specifications and quantities
sections.text: Assign unit U01 and part IDs such as P01. A panel row records material, thickness, dimension stage, face, edges, count and drawing reference. Distinguish a parts list from sheet purchasing: total part area alone does not establish sheet count without layout, grain, kerf and waste review. Separate hardware, finish and services with stated units.
sections.caption: Stable IDs connect drawings, part rows and quantity items.

sections.title: Calculate each line using matching units
sections.text: Training prices only: assume 2 sheets at 100 currency units each, 4 hardware sets at 15 per set, and 1 installation service at 40. Line totals are 200, 60 and 40; the total is 300 currency units. These are not market prices. Record quantity × matching unit price, currency, date, source and scope; do not multiply an area rate by a part count.
sections.caption: Training total: 2 × 100 + 4 × 15 + 1 × 40 = 300.

sections.title: Check scope and revision before issue
sections.text: Define included scope: finish already included in a faced-sheet rate must not be counted again for the same work. List transport, installation, tax and contingency as items or explicit exclusions without inventing universal percentages. Update dependent quantities when a unit changes and compare revisions. Mark an unpriced item as missing information rather than zero-cost work.
sections.caption: Scope checks prevent duplication; missing rates remain visible.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The training total was 300 currency units. Increasing hardware sets from 4 to 6 while other inputs stay fixed changes that line from 60 to 6 × 15 = 90. The revised total is 200 + 90 + 40 = 330. Record the 30 increase, revision and the exercise exclusion of transport.
example.decision: Decision: issue the revised 330 total with the 30 change and exclusions recorded.

quiz.question: What is the line total for 6 sets at 15 per set?

assignment.prompt: Prepare the three training lines in two revisions, with units, assumed prices, scope and cost change.

faq.question: Should an unknown rate be entered as zero?
faq.answer: Mark it as missing; zero can misleadingly imply free or included work.
